note: Translator: maintainer working Simple English. Hymn cluster.

primaries.primaryEn: Om. Of this Night-hymn of eight verses — seer Kuśika Saubhara (or Night Herself, daughter of Bharadvāja), deity Night, metre gāyatrī — the use is in Devī-Māhātmya reading. Om. Night approaches, the divine lady with many eyes. (Vedic Night-hymn 1, with padapāṭha.) In simple words the Veda's own night-prayer opens with its ritual seal — seer, goddess, metre, purpose — and the first cry: Night comes near, the all-seeing Goddess.
The goddess rises. Darkness. (Verse 2, padapāṭha fragments.) In simple words: She rises — and darkness (flees). These broken Vedic words are kept exactly as the old books carry them.
The goddess comes. Darkness. (Verse 3, padapāṭha fragments.) In simple words: She comes — and darkness (ends). Kept verbatim as handed down.

The Night-Goddess, all-pervading as the supreme principle, lights every object in every land for the senses; and She watches closely the good and bad deeds of the beings of the world She Herself bore, to fit each fruit. (Verse 1, Hindi.) Combined with the old note: to arrange each fruit She bears all powers. (Continued: immortal, all-pervading, light-destroying-darkness — next.)

This Goddess is deathless; pervading the whole world — creeping vines below, rising trees above — She stands; and with wisdom's light She destroys the darkness of ignorance in beings. (Verse 2, Hindi.) In simple words: undying Night fills everything from vine to treetop, and Her wisdom-light kills our inner dark.

May She be gracious to us today — She by whose coming we sleep happily in our homes, as birds sleep happily in tree-built nests at night. (Verse 4.) In simple words the prayer every home knows: as birds rest safe in nests at nightfall, so may we rest safe in our homes by Her grace — today itself.

Villages have gone to rest, walkers and birds have gone to rest — even need-driven hawks. (Verse 5.) In simple words night's lap gathers all: villagers, cattle, birds, moths, travelling strangers, even hunting hawks — all asleep in Her arms.

Keep the she-wolf from us, keep the wolf off; drive the thief away. Then be easy for us to cross. (Verse 6.) In simple words: O Night of consciousness-awareness, push desire-wolf and sin-wolf away from us, shoo the thief-band of lust — then become our easy crossing — giver of freedom, giver of blessing.

Near me has crept the dark, black, visible gloom. O Dawn — pay it off like a debt. (Verse 7.) Combined with the Vedic citation: Ṛgveda, book 10, chapter 10, hymn 127, mantras 1–8. In simple words: black ignorance-dark has crawled up to me, O Dawn-Goddess ruling the Night — clear it like a debt, as You clear devotees' debts with money, clear this dark with wisdom.

I have brought You praise as to a milch cow — choose, O daughter of heaven. O Night, accept our chant as You accepted our war-cries. (Verse 8.) In simple words: O Night, milch-cow-like Goddess, I come near with praise to win You over — daughter of the supreme Sky-Self! By Your grace I have already conquered lust and its army — now accept this offering too, as You accept battle-cries.

May the Night-Goddess be pleased with me now — on whose coming we sleep happily at home, as birds sleep happily in nest-homes at night. (Verse 4, Hindi.) Combined with the old prayer: in compassionate Night's lap, all village folk, foot-walking cows and horses, wing-flying birds and moths, need-driven travellers and hawks too sleep happily (5). O Night of consciousness-power, part from us the desire she-wolf and sin wolf; drive the lust-thief band far; then become our easy crossing — freedom-giving, blessing-making (6). O Dawn, O Night's ruling Goddess — all-spread black ignorance-dark has reached me; remove it like a debt — as giving wealth You clear devotees' debts, so giving wisdom clear this ignorance (7). O Night-Goddess, You are like a milch cow; approaching You with praise I win You over. Daughter of the supreme Sky-Self! By Your grace I have conquered lust and its foes — accept this oblation of mine too, like a chant. (8.)

In creation You are creation-formed, in keeping, keeping-formed; and in the end, ending-formed — O world-full Mother. (Tantrokta verse 5.) In simple words: at birth You are creation, in life You are maintenance, at the end You are dissolution — O Mother full of the world.

Great wisdom, great illusion, great memory, great recall; great delusion too — and great Goddess, great demon-slayer. (Verse 6.) In simple words Her fearsome roll-call: supreme learning, supreme magic, supreme memory, supreme mindfulness — and supreme delusion too; great Goddess, great killer of demons.

You are nature of all, three-qualities-showing; night-of-death, night-of-night, night-of-delusion — and terrible. (Verse 7.) In simple words: You are Mother Nature Herself, showing all three qualities — death-night, great-night, delusion-night — and dreadful.

You are Fortune, You are Ruler, You are modesty; You are mind marked by knowing. Shame and growth and gladness — You are peace, patience itself. (Verse 8.) In simple words every noble feminine power is Herself: wealth, command, modesty, understanding mind — shame, thriving, contentment — peace and forgiveness themselves.

Sword-lady, spear-lady, dreadful, mace-lady and discus-lady too; conch-lady, bow-lady, arrow, sling and club-weapons. (Verse 9.) In simple words the warrior roll-call: sword, spear, terror, mace, discus — conch, bow, arrows, fire-sling, iron club in hand.

Gentle, gentler than all gentle ones, lovelier still — supreme of high and low — You alone, supreme Lady. (Verse 10.) In simple words: gentlest of the gentle, most beautiful of beauties — higher than high and low — You alone are the supreme Queen.

Whatever thing, anywhere, real or not — O all-souled One — You are the power of it all; then how shall You be praised? (Verse 11.) In simple words the devotee gives up: everything real and unreal runs by Your power — so what words could ever praise You enough?

By whom the world-maker makes the world, who puts the world to sleep — even he was laid in sleep; who here is fit to praise You? (Verse 12.) In simple words: even Brahmā the maker works only through You, and even Viṣṇu You laid to sleep — so who in this world is worthy to praise You?

Viṣṇu, I, and the Lord Himself were made to take bodies by You — so who could have the power to praise You? (Verse 13.) In simple words: Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Śiva all took their bodies because You made them — then who has any strength left to praise You?

So praised, Goddess, with Your own generous glories — delude these two unattackable demons, Madhu-Kaiṭabha. (Verse 14.) In simple words Brahmā's plea turns practical: praised so with Your own noble powers — now enchant those two unassailable demons, Madhu and Kaiṭabha.

And quickly wake the world's Lord, the unfallen one; and make him aware — to kill these two great demons. (Verse 15.) In simple words: wake world-Lord Viṣṇu fast, fill Him with knowing — so He can kill these two mighty demons.

Thus ends the Night-hymn. Combined with the ritual note: before and after Saptashatī reading, apply the nine-lettered mantra with its placing, touching and picturing as told below. Victory to holy Gaṇapati. 'Om — of this holy nine-lettered mantra the seers are Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra, metres gāyatrī-uṣṇik-anuṣṭup, deities Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī; seed Aiṃ, power Hrīṃ, bolt Klīṃ — the use is in chanting to please Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī.' Having read it, sprinkle water. Then chanting each placing-word below, touch head, mouth, heart, secret, both feet and navel in turn with right-hand fingers. Seer-placing: salutation to seers Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra — on the head. To metres gāyatrī-uṣṇik-anuṣṭup — on the mouth. To deities Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī — on the heart. To seed Aiṃ — on the secret. To power Hrīṃ — on the feet. To bolt Klīṃ — on the navel. With the root-mantra 'Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce' purify the hands and do finger-placing. Finger-placing: Om Aiṃ to thumbs (forefingers touch both thumbs). Om Hrīṃ to forefingers (thumbs touch both forefingers). Om Klīṃ to middles (thumbs touch middles). Om Cāmuṇḍāyai to nameless (touch them). Om Vicce to littles (touch them). Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce to palm-and-back (palms touch each other's backs). Heart-and-limbs placing: here all five right-hand fingers touch 'heart' and the limbs. Om Aiṃ to heart (all five right fingers touch heart). Om Hrīṃ to head with 'hail'. Om Klīṃ to hair-top with 'vaṣaṭ'. Om Cāmuṇḍāyai to armour with 'hum' (right fingers touch left shoulder and left fingers right shoulder together). Om Vicce to three-eyes with 'vauṣaṭ' (fingertips touch both eyes and brow-centre). Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce to missile with 'phaṭ' (read this, swing right hand over the head from left-back to right-front, and clap left palm with fore-and-middle fingers). Letter-placing: reading each line below, touch hair-top and the rest with right-hand fingers. Om Aiṃ salutation — on hair-top. Om Hrīṃ — on right eye. Om Klīṃ — on left eye. Om Cāṃ — on right ear. Om Muṃ — on left ear. Om Ḍāṃ — on right nostril. Om Maiṃ(?) — on left nostril. Om Viṃ — on mouth. Ccе(?) — on secret. Thus placed, with the root-mantra pervade eight times (both hands touching all limbs head-to-foot), then snapping fingers in each direction, place with each line below — direction-placing: Om Aiṃ to east. Om Aiṃ to south-east. Om Hrīṃ to south. Om Hrīṃ to south-west. Om Klīṃ to west. Om Klīṃ to north-west. Om Cāmuṇḍāyai to north. Om Cāmuṇḍāyai to north-east. Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce to above. Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce to earth. (Page dust.) Picturing: sword, discus, mace, arrows, bow, club, spear, sling, head and corpse held in hands, three-eyed, dressed in all-limb jewels; dark-stone-glow, ten-faced-ten-footed — I serve great Kālikā, whom lotus-born Brahmā praised, while Viṣṇu slept, to kill Madhu and Kaiṭabha. (Verse 1.) Axe(?), hatchet(?), mace, arrows, thunderbolt, lotus, bow, flask, staff, spear, sword and shield, water-born, bell, gods' cup… (continues).

The Goddess who stands in all beings as power — to Her, salutation, salutation, salutation again and again. (Verse 12.) In simple words the great 'whoever-wherever' hymn begins: whatever being, whatever power works in it — that is Her; bow, bow, bow.

The Goddess who stands in all beings as thirst — to Her, salutation thrice and again. (Verse 13, with verse 14 quoted.) Combined with the old note: the Goddess who stands in all beings as patience — to Her, salutation thrice and again. (Verse 14.) In simple words: thirst that moves all creatures, patience that bears all creatures — both are Her; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as birth-form — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 15.) In simple words: every birth, every species-form — that is Her wearing forms; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as shame — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 16.) In simple words: the blush of shame that guards dignity in every heart — that is Her; bow.

The Goddess who stands in all beings as peace — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 17, with verse 18 quoted.) Combined with the old note: the Goddess who stands in all beings as faith — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 18.) In simple words: stillness of peace, and trustful faith — both are Her in every breast; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as beauty — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 19.) In simple words: every loveliness that delights the eye — that glow is Hers; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as fortune — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 20.) In simple words: every prosperity, every full house — Lakṣmī Herself in all beings; bow.

The Goddess who stands in all beings as conduct — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 21.) In simple words: every habit, every character, every way of living — all conduct is Her moving in beings; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as memory — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 22.) In simple words: all remembrance, all recognition — memory itself is Her; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as mercy — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 23.) In simple words: every melting of heart in pity — mercy itself is Her; bow.
The Goddess who stands in all beings as contentment — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 24.) In simple words: every 'enough, I am full' feeling — contentment itself is Her; bow.

The Goddess who stands in all beings as mother — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 25, with verse 26 quoted.) Combined with the old note: the Goddess who stands in all beings as error — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 26.) In simple words: every motherhood — and even every honest mistake that teaches — both are Her faces; bow.

Who stands in all beings and elements forever — to Her, pervading Goddess, salutation again and again. (Verse 27, with verse 28 quoted.) Combined with the old note: who as pure consciousness pervades and stands through all this world — to Her, salutation thrice and again. (Verse 28.) In simple words the closing seal: ruler of senses, dweller in elements, forever in all beings — O pervading consciousness-Goddess, salutation and salutation.

Praised by gods of old for wished shelter, and served by Indra-king day by day — may She make us good luck, O Queen, and smite our dangers. (Verse 29.) In simple words: gods praised Her for shelter since ancient days, Indra serves Her daily — may that Queen make our luck and kill our perils.

And now by us, baked by bold demons, and by gods bowing — remembered, She kills our dangers that very moment, through forms bowed low with love. (Verse 30.) In simple words the present-tense cry: now, by us scorched by proud demons and by bowing gods — the moment we remember, through Her love-bowed forms, She kills every danger of ours.

Then the mantra-share thinking, in brief and in full. (Mantra-division note, with old gloss.) Combined with the old note: some wish 'Om salutation to Caṇḍikā' to be a separate mantra — but then the saying 'from ma-letter to ṃ-letter' would break, and which 'Goddess-said' mantra to drop stays undecided; that view too is gathered and set down in the hundred-verse garland with eight good verses. In simple words a scholar's footnote on counting mantras — kept exactly as the edition carries it.
Gathered in the hundred-verse garland with eight good verses. (Mantra-share note, verse 72.) In simple words: this counting is collected in the hundred-verse manual with eight fine verses.

'Three less among speech-mantras; in halves, the rite-knowers; twenty in verse-count; chapters too are mantras.' (Verse 73.) In simple words the counting-riddle continues: speech-spells fall three short, half-verses hold the rite-masters, twenty in verse-tally — and the chapters themselves are mantras.

At start and end, sixteen and sixteen tellings of the nine-lettered; one extra in the verse-heap; all the rest as before. (Verse 74.) In simple words: sixteen nine-lettered tellings at the beginning, sixteen at the end; one verse extra in the heap; everything else as before.

For the first merchant is missing at the start, and the last sage too; 'in love, by Your praise-battle' — a half-verse mantra-soul. (Verse 75.) In simple words the fine counting: the first merchant-verse and the last sage-verse drop out at the start; 'in love, by Your praise-battle' stands as a half-verse mantra-heart.

'Kill us two' — before the half, in the fifth no goddess-voice; in the tenth, 'blazed' and the rest — the last mantra-sense is extra. (Verse 76.) In simple words the last counting-knots: before 'kill us two', the fifth chapter carries no goddess-voice; in the tenth, 'they blazed' and the rest — the final mantra-sense stands extra.

Yet Your matchless love for me — for a bad son may somewhere be born, but a bad mother never is. (Verse 4.) In simple words the poet's anchor-line, famous across India: sons may turn out bad, but a mother is never bad — and that is why Your incomparable love still falls on me.

Gods cast aside, busy with many kinds of service — and my age past eighty-five. If now, O Mother, Your grace comes not, support-less — O birth-giver of the pot-bellied one! — whose shelter shall I go to? (Verse 5, with verse 6 quoted.) Combined with the old note: an outcaste chatterer becomes, by one mantra-letter entering the ear, a sweet speaker like honey-food; the penniless roams long fearless with crores of gold. If hearing one letter bears such fruit, what must the full fruit of rite-done chanting be — what man can know? (Verse 6.) In simple words the old poet confesses: eighty-five years spent serving other gods, all now left behind, no strength left — Mother, if even now You won't look at me, support-less, where shall I go? And remember: even one heard letter of Your mantra turns a fool's tongue honey-sweet and a beggar fearless-rich — then who can measure full chanting's fruit?

O leaf-clad One! Into the ear, on mantra-letter-fruit: what man knows what must be chanted in chanting's rite? (Verse 6, with Śiva's praise following.) In simple words: O Aparṇā (leaf-unclad), if one heard letter fruits so hugely — who can know the fruit of full rite-done chanting? (Then the hymn turns to Śiva, exalted by wedding You.)

This was never right for You — for in this world a bad son may be, but nowhere a bad mother. (Verse 3, Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: O Mother, O world-Mother, never did I serve Your feet, nor offer You much wealth — yet on wretch-like me You pour matchless love. Why? Because in this world a bad son may be born, but nowhere is there a bad mother. (Verse 4.) In simple words the poet argues his case: I gave You nothing — yet You love me; and that is only right, for bad sons exist, bad mothers never.

Ash-smeared limbs, poison for food, sky-clad, matted, snake-king-garlanded on the throat, skull in hand — yet the Lord of ghosts holds the one title 'Lord of the world'. Bhavānī! This is the fruit of wedding-custom with You. (Verse 7.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: He who smears pyre-ash on limbs, eats poison, wears sky (naked), knots His hair, garlands snake-king Vāsuki on the throat, and shines a skull in hand — that ghost-Lord Paśupati, how did He win the single title 'Lord of the world'? What made Him great? Only the fruit of wedding-custom with You — marrying You raised Him. (Verse 7.) In simple words: Śiva the beggar-ascetic became Jagadīśa the world-Lord for one reason only — He married You.

Moon-faced Mother! I want no freedom, nor world-glory want, nor wisdom-seeking, nor joy again. So I beg You, Mother — let my birth pass chanting: Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Śiva, Śiva, Bhavānī. (Verse 8, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee refuses every bargain — no liberation, no riches, no knowledge, not even happiness. One begging only: Mother, let my whole life pass chanting Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Śiva, Śiva, Bhavānī.

Never worshipped duly with many offerings; what was left undone by harsh-thinking words? Yet, O dark One, if You Yourself hold some mercy on helpless me — O Mother, that alone befits You supremely. (Verse 9, Hindi, with page dust.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: O dark Mother Śyāmā, never did I worship You duly with full ritual things; harsh-minded, my words left no fault undone. Yet You Yourself take pains to hold a little mercy-glance on helpless me — Mother, only You suit such grace. (Only a mother like You could shelter a son like me.) (Verse 9.)

What must the full fruit of rite-done chanting be — who can know? (Verse 6, Hindi seal.) In simple words the wonder stands: if one heard letter does all that — who can measure the fruit of full, rite-done chanting? No one.

What made ghost-Lord Paśupati the one 'Lord of the world'? Only wedding You. (Verse 7, Hindi seal.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: ash-smeared, poison-eating, sky-clad, matted, snake-garlanded, skull-handed — yet titled sole Jagadīśa. Why? How did He win such greatness? Only as fruit of wedding-custom with You — marrying You raised Him. (Verse 7.) In simple words the proof is repeated slowly: the beggar-god became world-Lord by one wedding — Yours.

No freedom I want, no world-glory, no wisdom-seeking, no joy — only this I beg: let my birth pass chanting 'Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Śiva, Śiva, Bhavānī'. (Verse 8, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee's only bargain restated: take everything else — leave me just Your names on my tongue for life.

O dark Mother Śyāmā, never did I worship You duly with full ritual things; harsh-minded, my words left no fault undone. Yet You Yourself take pains to hold a little mercy-glance on helpless me — Mother, only You suit such grace. (Only a mother like You could shelter a son like me.) (Verse 9, Hindi.) In simple words: I never worshipped right, my words were harsh, my faults complete — yet You Yourself bother to glance kindly at helpless me. Mother, such grace suits only You.

O Mother of the world! If Your full mercy stays on me — what wonder is here? For a mother never overlooks a son heaped fault on fault. (Verse 11.) In simple words: Mother, if Your whole mercy rests on me — no wonder at all. A mother never abandons even a son piled with fault upon fault.

No sinner like me; no sin-killer like You. Knowing so, O great Goddess, do as befits. (Verse 12, with verse 11's Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: O Mother of the world, if Your full mercy stays on me — no wonder; a mother never overlooks even a fault-heaped son (11). O great Goddess, no sinner equals me, and no sin-remover equals You — knowing this, do what is fit. (12.) In simple words the final bargain: I am the worst sinner, You the best sin-remover — matched perfectly; now do what fits.
Thus ends the fault-forgiveness hymn composed by holy Śaṅkarācārya. (Colophon.) In simple words the seal: so closes the Goddess-fault-forgiveness hymn, made by Śrī Śaṅkarācārya himself.

O Mother Durgā! Ocean of mercy, great Queen! Caught in dangers, I now remember You (never before) — don't count it as slyness; for hunger-thirst pained children remember Mother. (Verse 10, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee answers the unspoken charge: yes, I remember You only now in danger — don't call it cunning; hungry-thirsty children always cry for Mother.

O Mother of the world, if Your full mercy stays on me — no wonder; a mother never overlooks even a fault-heaped son. (Verse 11, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: O great Goddess, no sinner equals me, and no sin-remover equals You — knowing this, do what is fit. (12.) In simple words mercy as mother-logic: full mercy on me is no miracle — mothers never abandon fault-heaped sons; and since I am the worst sinner and You the best remover, deal with me fittingly.

Remembered by the healthy, You give wisdom most blest; O poverty-pain-fear-stealer — who but You, ever-melting heart for helping all? (Verse 2.) In simple words the seven-verse Durgā opens mid-praise: remembered, You take all beings' fear; thought on by the hale, You grant most holy wisdom; stealer of want, pain and fear — who but You stays ever soft-hearted to help all?

O all-blessing-blessed! Śivā! fulfiller of all aims! Refuge! Three-eyed! Fair One! Nārāyaṇī! salutation to You. (Verse 3.) In simple words the beloved all-name garland: blessing of blessings, gentle giver, fulfiller of every human aim, shelter, three-eyed, fair — O Nārāyaṇī, salutation.

O sheltered-poor-pained-rescuer, devoted! O all-pain-stealer of all! Goddess! Nārāyaṇī! salutation to You. (Verse 4.) In simple words: devoted rescuer of sheltered poor and pained, stealer of every pain of all — O Goddess Nārāyaṇī, salutation.

O all-formed! All-Lady! All-power-holding! From fears guard us, Goddess! Durgā! Goddess! salutation to You. (Verse 5.) In simple words: every form, every Lordship, every power in one — guard us from all fears, O Goddess Durgā, salutation.

All diseases You wipe, pleased; angered, You wipe all wished joys. Yours sheltered never face ruin — Yours sheltered shelter others. (Verse 6.) In simple words the two-faced promise: pleased, You destroy every disease; angered, You destroy every wished joy. Those sheltered in You never meet ruin — and Yours go on sheltering others.

O Mother Durgā! Remembered, You steal all beings' fear; thought on by healthy men, You grant most holy wisdom. O stealer of pain, poverty and fear — who but You stays ever kindly-melted to help all? (Verse 2, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats slowly: remembered — fear gone for all beings; meditated by the healthy — holiest wisdom given; pain-poverty-fear stolen — and who but You stays forever soft-hearted to help everyone?

O Nārāyaṇī! Giver of all blessings, blessed Yourself; gentle Śivā; fulfiller of all human aims; lover of the sheltered. (Verse 3, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: three-eyed and fair — salutation to You. (Verse 3.) In simple words the name-garland in Hindi: all-blessing, blessed, gentle, aim-fulfilling, shelter-loving, three-eyed, fair — O Nārāyaṇī, salutation.

Rescuer ever busy saving sheltered poor and pained, remover of everyone's pain — O Goddess Nārāyaṇī, salutation. (Verse 4, Hindi.) In simple words: always on duty saving the sheltered poor and suffering, wiping every pain — O Nārāyaṇī Goddess, salutation.

All-formed, All-Queen, holding every power — divine-formed Durgā Goddess, guard us from all fears; salutation. (Verse 5, Hindi.) In simple words: every form, every queenship, every power — divine Durgā — guard us from every fear; salutation.

O Goddess, pleased You destroy all diseases, angered You destroy all wished joys. Those gone to Your shelter never meet ruin — gone to Your shelter, men become shelters for others. (Verse 6, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: sheltered ones become shelters. (Verse 6.) In simple words the turning-point promise: Your sheltered never fall — and more, they themselves become shelter for others.

O all-worlds' whole-Lady! All trouble-quelling of the triple world — so too by You be done: our foes' destruction. (Verse 7.) In simple words the closing errand: O Queen of everything, as You calm every trouble of all three worlds — so destroy our enemies too.

Thus ends holy seven-verse Durgā. O whole-Queen, calm all troubles of the triple world as ever, and destroy our foes. (Verse 7, Hindi, with closer.) Combined with the closer: thus ends holy seven-verse Durgā. Thus ends holy seven-verse Durgā — complete. In simple words the seal is stamped twice for certainty: the seven verses are complete; and the prayer stands — calm all troubles, kill our foes.

Then the hundred-and-eight-name hymn: the Lord speaks — 'I shall tell the hundred names; listen, lotus-faced. By whose grace alone pleased Durgā becomes.' (Verse 1.) In simple words Śiva turns to Pārvatī: lotus-faced One, now hear the hundred names — by whose grace-reading alone good Durgā is pleased.

Om. Satī, Sādhvī, dear to Becoming, Bhavānī, Becoming-freeing; Noble, Durgā, Victorious and First; Three-eyed, Spear-bearing. (Verse 2.) In simple words the name-count begins: Satī 1, Sādhvī 2, Becoming-lover 3, Bhavānī 4, world-freeing 5, Noble 6, Durgā 7, Victorious 8, First 9, Three-eyed 10, Spear-bearing 11.

Bow-bearer, Bright, fierce-belled, greatly penanced; Mind, Thought, I-sense, and mind-formed, pyre and knowing. (Verse 3.) In simple words the count continues: bow-bearing 12, bright 13, fierce-belled 14, great in penance 15; mind 16, thought 17, I-sense 18, mind-formed 19, pyre 20, knowing 21.

All-mantras-formed, being, truth-bliss-formed; endless, becoming, to-be-become, well-to-be, non-to-be, ever-going. (Verse 4, with name-list note.) Combined with the name-gloss note: Om Satī 1, Sādhvī 2, Becoming-lover (loving Lord Śaṅkara) 3, Bhavānī 4, world-freeing (freeing from world-bond) 5, Noble 6, Durgā 7, Victorious 8, First 9 (meant: First 9), Three-eyed 10, Spear-bearing 11, bow-bearing 12, Bright 13, fierce-belled (fierce-voiced bell-ringing) 14, greatly penanced (heavy penance-doing) 15, Mind (thinking power) 16, Thought (knowing power) 17, I-sense (I-ness's shelter) 18, mind-formed 19, pyre 20, knowing (consciousness) 21, all-mantras-formed 22, Being (continues next).

Śaṅkara said to Pārvatī: lotus-faced One, now I shall tell the hundred-and-eight names — hear them; by whose grace-reading alone good Durgā is pleased. Hear. (Verse 1, Hindi, with name-list.) Combined with the full name-gloss continuing: Being 23, truth-bliss-formed 24, endless (whose form ends nowhere) 25, becoming (birthing all) 26, to-be-become (continues next).
Aditi gave birth — the Goddess impel! (Verse 12, Vedic fragments.) In simple words broken Vedic words kept holy: Aditi bore — may the Goddess urge us on.
O Dakṣa! Your daughter Aditi — from Her deathless blissful gods were born. (Verse 13.) In simple words: O Dakṣa, your daughter Aditi gave birth — and from Her came the death-free, blessed gods.

Desire, womb, Fortune, thunder-handed, cave, laughter, wind-carried, cloud, Indra. Again cave, all, with illusion — and to the All, this world-mother, first-wisdom, Om. (Verse 14, code-mantra.) Combined with the old note: the speech-formed blessing Goddess, pleased with fine praise, draw near us. (Verse 10.) Time-destroying, Veda-praised Viṣṇu-power, war-god-mother (Śiva-power), Sarasvatī (Brahmā-power), gods'-mother Aditi and Dakṣa's daughter… (continues). In simple words the famous code-mantra unrolled in Hindi: desire (ka), womb (e), Fortune (ī), thunder-handed Indra (la), cave (hrīṃ), laughter-sound (ha), sa-letters, wind-borne (ka), cloud (ha), Indra (la), cave again (hrīṃ), sa-ka-la letters, and illusion (hrīṃ) — this is the All-souled world-Mother's root wisdom, Brahman-formed. (Verse 14.)

O Dakṣa! Your daughter Aditi gave birth, and from Her death-free blessed gods were born. (Verse 13, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats: Dakṣa's daughter Aditi became mother — and bore the deathless blessed gods.

Desire, womb, Fortune, thunder-handed, cave, laughter, wind, cloud, Indra — cave again, all, with illusion: this All-souled world-Mother's root wisdom, Brahman-formed. (Verse 14, Hindi, with great gloss.) Combined with the great gloss: Śiva-power-non-different-formed, Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva-souled, Sarasvatī-Lakṣmī-Gaurī-formed, impure-mixed-pure-worship-formed, клад… (continues). In simple words the mantra's ocean-meaning begins: one-with-Śiva, Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva in one body… (continues next).

She is Self-power. She is world-charmer. Noose-goad-bow-arrow-bearing. She is holy great-wisdom. Who knows thus crosses grief. (Verse 15.) In simple words the Upaniṣad's drum-beat: She is the Self's own power; She charms the whole world; noose, goad, bow, arrow in hand; She is holy supreme wisdom — whoever knows this crosses over grief.
Salutation to You, O Blessed Lady! Mother, guard us on every side. (Verse 16.) In simple words the child's cry: salutations, blessed Mother — guard us all around.

She alone is the eight Vasus. She alone the eleven Rudras. She alone the twelve suns. She alone the All-gods, soma-drinkers and not. She alone the sorcerers, demons, ghosts, goblins, sprites, perfected. She alone the three qualities. She alone Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-formed. She alone lord-makers, Indra, Manus. She alone planets, stars, lights. Time-formed as minute-moment and the rest. Her I salute daily — sin-stealing Goddess, joy-freedom-giving, endless, victorious, pure, shelter-worthy, bliss-giving, blessed. (Verse 17.) In simple words the great 'She alone' litany: eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve suns, all gods, all demons and spirits, all qualities, the Trinity, law-givers, planets and stars and Time itself — She alone is every one of them; and that sin-stealing, joy-and-freedom-giving, endless, victorious, pure, sheltering, blissful, blessed Goddess — I salute daily.

Sky-letter-joined, fire-mingled, half-moon-glittering — the Goddess's seed, fulfilling every aim. (Verse 18.) In simple words the seed-sound decoded: sky (ha) joined with ī, fire (ra) mingled, crescent-moon crowned — the Goddess's seed Hrīṃ, fulfilling every wish.

Separate limbs shown apart, tangled-knowingly told — hence know how secret and weighty these mantras are. (Verse 18's seal, Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: these are the Self's power; world-charming; noose-goad-bow-arrow-bearing; holy supreme wisdom — whoever knows thus crosses grief. (Verse 15.) In simple words the editors marvel: limb by limb shown separately, tangled on purpose — see from this how secret and heavy these mantras are.

Blessed Lady, salutation! Mother, guard us every way. (Verse 16, Hindi, with seer-note.) Combined with the seer-note: She alone is the eight Vasus; She alone the eleven Rudras, the twelve suns; She alone the soma-drinking and non-drinking All-gods; She alone the sorcerers, demons, ghosts, goblins, sprites and perfected; She alone goodness-passion-darkness; She alone Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-formed; She alone lord-makers, Indra, Manus; She alone planets, stars and lights; She alone minute-moment-time-formed; that sin-destroying, joy-freedom-giving, endless, victory-dwelling, spotless, shelter-fit, bliss-giving, blessed Goddess we salute ever. (Verse 17.) In simple words: salutation, blessed Mother — guard us every way; and the whole 'She alone' litany in Hindi — Vasus, Rudras, suns, All-gods, demons-spirits, qualities, Trinity, law-givers, planets-stars-Time — that sin-killing, joy-freeing, endless, victorious, pure, sheltering, blissful blessed Goddess we salute daily.

Sky (ha) and ī-joined, fire (ra)-mingled, crescent-crowned — the Goddess's seed Hrīṃ fulfils every wish. (Verse 18, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the decoding slowly: sky-letter plus ī, fire-letter mixed in, half-moon on top — Goddess-seed Hrīṃ, fulfiller of every desire.

Thus the one-letter Brahman pure-hearted strivers picture — supreme-bliss-full, wisdom-ocean-hearts. (Verse 19.) In simple words: the one-letter Brahman (Hrīṃ) — pure-hearted strivers full of topmost bliss, oceans of wisdom — picture It so.

Speech-seed, illusion-seed, Brahman-womb, desire-seed; then sixth-with-mouth-joined. (Verse 20, with code-line quoted.) Combined with the quoted code: sun, unwrong-ear-drop-joined, from ṭa the third. (Verse 20.) In simple words the nine-lettered code begins unrolling: speech (Aiṃ), illusion (Hrīṃ), Brahman-womb-desire (Klīṃ), then the sixth consonant mouth-joined… (continues next).

With Nārāyaṇa mixed, and wind with lower-joined — then: may the nine-lettered letter grant great bliss-giving. (Verse 20, code completion.) In simple words the code completes: mixed with Nārāyaṇa-vowel, wind with lower-vowel — then 'Vicce': may the nine-lettered mantra grant great bliss.

Heart-lotus-centred, dawn-sun-glowing; noose-goad-bearing, gentle, boon-fearlessness-handed; three-eyed, red-robed, devotee-wish-cowing — I serve. (Verse 21.) In simple words the dawn-picture to hold: heart-lotus-centred, glowing like morning sun, noose-goad in hand, gentle, boon-and-fearless hands, three eyes, red robes — wish-cow to devotees — I serve Her.

Thus this one-letter Brahman (Hrīṃ) is pictured by strivers of pure heart, topmost-bliss-full, oceans of wisdom. (This mantra counts as Goddess-breath. Like Om-sound, this breath too is full of spread meaning. In brief its sense is: wish-knowledge-action-bearing, non-dual, unbroken, true-being-bliss, same-tasting, Śiva-power-flashing.) (Verse 19, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats: pure-hearted, bliss-full, wisdom-ocean strivers picture the one-letter Brahman so — and this mantra is the Goddess's own Om: brief sense — will-wisdom-action in one, non-dual, whole, true-bliss, one-tasting, Śiva-power-flashing.

Speech (Aiṃ), illusion (Hrīṃ), Brahman-womb-desire (Klīṃ); then sixth consonant, that is cha, mouth-joined (chā); sun (ma); 'unwrong ear' — right ear (u) drop-joined (muṃ); from ṭa the third, ḍa, mixed with Nārāyaṇa-vowel ā (ḍā); wind (ya) lower-joined, that is ai (yai); and 'Vicce' — may this nine-lettered mantra grant joy and Brahman-union to seekers. (Verse 20, Hindi decoding.) Combined with the mantra-sense: O consciousness-formed Mahāsarasvatī! O being-formed Mahālakṣmī! O bliss-formed Mahākālī! To win Brahman-wisdom we all picture You ever. O Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī-formed Caṇḍikā, salutation to You. Open the ignorance-rope's tight knot and free me. (Verse 20.) In simple words letter by letter the code is opened, then its heart-prayer: O wisdom-formed Sarasvatī, O being-formed Lakṣmī, O bliss-formed Kālī — for Brahman-wisdom we picture You always; O three-formed Caṇḍikā, salutation — untie ignorance's tight rope-knot and free me.

Heart-lotus-centred, dawn-sun-glowing, noose-goad-bearing, gentle-formed, boon-fearless-handed, three-eyed, red-robed, devotee-wish-cowing Goddess — I serve. (Verse 21, Hindi.) In simple words the dawn-picture repeated slowly: heart-lotus seat, morning-sun glow, noose and goad, gentle face, blessing and fearless hands, three eyes, red robes — wish-cow to devotees — I serve.

I bow to You, great Goddess, great-fear-destroying; great-hardship-quelling, great-mercy-formed. (Verse 22.) In simple words the bow: great Goddess, destroyer of great fears, queller of great hardships, formed of great mercy — I bow to You.

Whose form even Brahmā and the rest know not — hence called Unknowable. Whose end is never got — hence called Endless. Whose aim never shows — hence called Unseeable. Whose birth never appears — hence called Unborn. Alone everywhere abiding — hence called One. Alone world-formed — hence called Not-one. So called Unknowable-Endless-Unseeable-Unborn-One-Not-one. (Verse 23.) In simple words six names decoded from Her nature: unknown to Brahmā and the rest — so Unknowable; never ending — so Endless; never aimed-at — so Unseeable; never born — so Unborn; alone everywhere — so One; alone world-formed — so Many.

Of mantras the Mother-goddess, of words wisdom-formed; of knowings beyond-consciousness, of voids the void-witness. Than whom naught is higher — She is famed Durgā. (Verse 24.) In simple words the definition-seal: Mother of mantras, wisdom of words, beyond-consciousness of knowings, witness of voids — and Она beyond whom nothing higher stands — She is famed as Durgā.

To that Durgā hard-to-reach, Goddess, ill-conduct-destroying — I bow, world-fearing, world-sea-ferrying. (Verse 25.) In simple words the frightened devotee's bow: to hard Durgā, Goddess, killer of ill-conduct — I, scared of the world, bow — ferry me over the world-sea.

Whoever studies this Atharva-top wins five Atharva-top-chant fruits. (Verse 26, with Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: destroyer of great fears, queller of great hardships, very mercy-formed — I bow to You, great Goddess. (Verse 22.) In simple words the fruit begins: whoever studies this Atharva-top wins the fruit of five Atharva-top chantings.

Whose form Brahmā and the rest know not — hence Unknowable; whose end is never got — hence Endless; whose aim never shows — hence Unseeable; whose birth never appears — hence Unborn; alone everywhere — hence One; alone world-formed — hence Many. So called. (Verse 23, Hindi.) In simple words the six-name decoding repeated slowly: unknown — Unknowable; unending — Endless; unseen-aimed — Unseeable; unborn — Unborn; alone everywhere — One; alone world-formed — Many.

In all mantras 'Mother' — root-letter-formed indwelling; in words, wisdom (sense)-formed indwelling; in knowings, 'beyond-consciousness'; in voids, 'void-witness'; and than whom naught is higher — famed as Durgā. (Verse 24, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: a variant 'bliss-consciousness' reading also fits well. In simple words: Mother of mantras as root-letters, wisdom of words as sense, beyond-mind of knowings, witness of voids — and higher than whom nothing — famed Durgā.

To hard, ill-conduct-killing, world-sea-ferrying Durgā Goddess — world-scared, I bow. (Verse 25, Hindi.) In simple words the scared devotee bows again: hard Durgā, conduct 청… — to ill-conduct-killing, world-sea-ferrying Durgā — scared of the world, I bow.

Whoever studies this Atharva-top wins five Atharva-top-chant fruits. Without knowing it, whoever sets up an image — even chanting a hundred lakh times — wins no image-power. Hundred-eight is told as its fore-rite. Whoever reads ten times is freed of sins at once. Crosses great hardships by great Goddess's grace. (Verse 26.) In simple words the rule and fruit: study brings fivefold fruit; image-setting without knowing it fails even after crore-chantings; 108 is its fore-rite; ten readings free sins instantly; by great Goddess's grace, cross the hardest hardships.

Evening-reading destroys day-made sin. Morning-reading destroys night-made sin. Both-times user becomes sinless. Midnight, fourth-twilight chanting wins speech-power. On a new image chanting brings god-presence. At breath-fixing, chanting fixes breaths. On earth-star (deathless-yoga) chanting in great Goddess's nearness crosses great death. Who knows thus crosses great death. Thus the Upaniṣad. (Verses 26–27.) In simple words the timetable of fruits: evening reading kills day-sins, morning kills night-sins, both-times makes sinless; midnight fourth-twilight chant wins speech-powers; on a new image wins god-nearness; at breath-installing wins breath-fixing; on deathless-yoga days in Her nearness crosses great death — whoever knows this crosses great death. Thus ends the Upaniṣad.

Evening study kills day-sins; morning study kills night-sins. Both-times study makes sinless. Midnight fourth-twilight chant wins speech-power. New-image chant wins god-nearness. Breath-fixing chant fixes breaths. Earth-star deathless-yoga chanting in Her nearness crosses great death. Whoever knows thus crosses great death. Thus this ignorance-killing Brahman-wisdom. (Verses 26–27, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the timetable slowly: evening kills day's sins, morning kills night's, both make sinless; midnight wins speech-power; new image wins nearness; breath-rite wins breath-fixing; deathless-yoga wins over great death — whoever knows crosses great death. Thus this ignorance-killing Brahman-wisdom.

Without knowing this Atharva-top, image-setting wins no image-power even after crore-chantings. Hundred-eight is its fore-rite. Ten readings free sins instantly and cross great hardships by Her grace. (Verse 26, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: 108 chantings and the rest is its fore-rite. Whoever reads ten times is freed of sins that very moment and crosses great hardships by Her grace. (Verse 26.) In simple words the rule restated: no knowing, no image-power — even crores of chantings fail; 108 is the fore-rite; ten readings free sins on the spot and cross the hardest hardships.

I wish to know this highest practice of mine — Brahman-union-birthing, told by You, O Lord! (Śakti-mystery 1.) In simple words the Goddess Herself asks: Lord, I wish to learn my own supreme practice — the one You told, which births union with Brahman.

What is its rule, by what path the practice, what mantra is ordained here, and what of picturing-worship and the rest? (Verse 2.) In simple words Her four questions: what is the rule? which path? which mantra? what picturing and worship?

Holy Sadāśiva speaks: hear, O greatly-fortuned Goddess! Your worship's cause — by serving which, Brahman-union one wins. (Verse 3.) In simple words the Lord answers: greatly blessed Goddess, hear the cause of Your worship — serving which, one wins Brahman-union.

You are supreme nature itself of Brahman, supreme Self. From You was born the whole world — You are the world's mother, O blessed! (Verse 4.) In simple words the Lord's praise begins: You are nature supreme of Brahman the supreme Self; from You the whole world was born — You are the world's mother, O blessed One.

From first-matter to atom-end, this moving-unmoving all — by You alone was birthed, O blessed! This world rests on You. (Verse 5.) In simple words: from cosmic root-matter down to the tiniest atom, all moving-unmoving — You alone birthed it, blessed One; this world leans on You.

You are first of all wisdoms, birth-ground even of us. You know the whole world — You no one knows. (Verse 6.) In simple words: first of all sacred learnings, birthplace even of us gods — You know everything, and no one knows You.

You are Kālī, Rescuer, Durgā; Sixteen, World-Queen. Smoke-robed, Crane-faced, Bhairavī, Beheaded. (Verse 7.) In simple words the ten wisdom-goddesses hailed as Herself: Kālī, Tārā (rescuer), Durgā, Ṣoḍaśī, Bhuvaneśvarī — Smoke-veiled, Crane-faced Bheruṇḍā, Bhairavī, Chinnamastā.

You are food-full, speech-Goddess; O Goddess, lotus-homed. All-power-formed are You, all-gods-bodied. (Verse 8.) In simple words the praise pours on: food-full Annapūrṇā, speech-goddess Vāṇī, lotus-homed Lakṣmī — all powers in form, all gods in body.

You alone are subtle, gross are You — manifest-unmanifest-formed. Formless yet formed — who deserves to know You? (Verse 9.) In simple words the wonder: subtle alone, gross alone, seen-unseen-formed — formless yet formed — who is fit to know You?

You are all-formed Goddess, highest mother of all; pleased, when You are, O Queen of gods — all are pleased. (Verse 10.) In simple words: all-formed Goddess, highest mother of all — Queen of gods, when You are pleased, everyone is pleased.

At creation's start You alone were — dark-formed, beyond reach. From You was born the whole world, by Absolute wishing to make. (Verse 11, page dust.) In simple words: before making, You alone were — dark-formed, out of reach; from You the whole world was born when the Absolute wished to create. (Running page number follows.)

From first-matter to elements-end, this world by You was made; the Absolute Brahman a mere nudge — cause of all causes. (Verse 12.) In simple words: from cosmic root to last element You made this world; Brahman the Absolute stood only as the nudge — the cause behind all causes.

Being-formed, everywhere-spread, covering all It stands; ever-one-formed, mere-consciousness, unstained among all things. (Verse 13.) In simple words that Absolute praised: being itself, spread everywhere, covering all, ever one-formed, pure consciousness — unstained by anything.

It acts not, eats not, goes not, stands not; true, wise, beginning-endless, beyond word-mind-reach. (Verse 14.) In simple words: It does nothing, eats nothing, goes nowhere, stands nowhere — true, knowing, beginningless-endless, beyond words and mind.

Holding only Its wish, You — supreme great-yoginī — make, keep and at the end kill this moving-unmoving world. (Verse 15.) In simple words: holding just Its wish as support, You — supreme great Yoginī — make, keep and finally dissolve this moving-unmoving world.

Your form is Great Time, world-destroying; at great-dissolution time, Time shall swallow all. (Verse 16.) In simple words: Your form is Mahākāla, world-destroyer — at final dissolution, Time will swallow everything.

From swallowing all beings, Great Time is famed; from swallowing Great Time, You are first, supreme Kālī. (Verse 17.) In simple words the name decoded: swallowing all beings — hence Great Time; swallowing Great Time — hence You, first supreme Kālī.

From time-swallowing, Kālī, first-formed of all; by time-ness, by first-beingness, first Kālī is sung. (Verse 18.) In simple words sung again: time-swallower, first-formed of all — by time-ness, by first-ness — first Kālī is sung.

Then, reaching Her own form — dark-formed, formless; beyond words, mind-reached — You alone are left. (Verse 19.) In simple words the end as the beginning: then, regaining Her own form — dark-formed, formless, beyond words yet reached by mind — You alone remain.

Formed yet formless, by illusion many-formed; You beginningless of all, beginningless — maker here, and keeper. (Verse 20.) In simple words: formed yet formless, many-formed by illusion — beginning of all, beginningless Yourself — maker here and keeper.

You are first, supreme power, all-power-formed; by Your power we are strong in making-keeping-melting and the rest. (Verse 21.) In simple words: first supreme power, all powers in form — by Your power even we gods are strong for making, keeping, melting and all.

Your forms are endless, many-hued-shaped; by many hard efforts, who can tell them? (Verse 22.) In simple words: endless Your forms, many-hued, many-shaped — won only by many hard efforts — who can ever tell them all?

You world-mother Durgā, birth-world-freeing; You first, world's nurse, keeper, higher-than-high. (Verse 23.) In simple words: world-mother Durgā, freeing from birth-world; first One, world's nurse, keeper, higher than the high.

By You alone is held, O Goddess, this moving-unmoving world; You alone are earth, waters, wind, fire. (Verse 24, hymn continues.) In simple words: by You alone this moving-unmoving world is held — earth alone, waters alone, wind alone, fire alone are You. (The hymn continues beyond this batch.)

O Pārvatī! Guard this like your own womb, with effort — this finest Kuñjikā-hymn, by mere reading, fulfils killing, charming, mastering, stilling and expelling aims. (Verse 4, Hindi seal of the mantra.) In simple words Śiva warns: keep this Kuñjikā hymn secret like your own body — mere reading of it fulfils the five fierce aims.

The mantra: 'Om Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce. Om Glaum Hum Klīṃ Jūṃ Saḥ — blaze, blaze, burn, burn, flare, flare — Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce — blaze, kindle, burn, burn, flare, flare — Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Cāmuṇḍāyai Vicce — blaze. Haṃ Saṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Phaṭ, hail.' Thus the mantra. Salutation to Rudra-formed! Salutation to honey-demon-killer! Salutation to Kaiṭabha-destroyer! Salutation to buffalo-crusher! (Verse 1.) In simple words the Kuñjikā seed-mantra blazes forth with fire-sounds — then four salutations: Rudra-formed, honey-demon-killer, Kaiṭabha-destroyer, buffalo-crusher.

Salutation to Śumbha-killer and Niśumbha-demon-slayer! (Verse 2, with verse 3 quoted.) Combined with the old note: make my chanting awake and perfect, O great Goddess! Creation-formed by Aiṃ-sound, guarding by Hrīṃ-sound. (Verse 3.) In simple words: salutation to the slayer of Śumbha and Niśumbha — and: O great Goddess, wake my chanting and perfect it; by Aiṃ-sound creation-formed… (continues next).

Salutation to Klīṃ-formed desire-formed, seed-formed! Cāmuṇḍā, Caṇḍa-slayer, and Yai-formed boon-giver. (Verse 4.) In simple words each seed is hailed: Klīṃ-formed desire, seed-form itself; Caṇḍa-slaying Cāmuṇḍā; Yai-formed boon-giver — salutation.

And Vicce-formed forever fear-giving — salutation to mantra-formed! (Verse 5, with verse 6 quoted.) Combined with the old note: Dhāṃ Dhīṃ Dhūṃ-formed wife of matted-locked Śiva; Vāṃ Vīṃ Vaṃ-formed queen of speech. Krāṃ Krīṃ Krū-formed Goddess Kālī; Śāṃ Śīṃ Śūṃ — do my good. (Verse 6.) In simple words: Vicce-formed, forever fear-removing, mantra-formed Goddess — salutation; then seed after seed is hailed — Dhūrjaṭī’s wife, speech-queen, Kālī — ending: do my good.

Huṃ Huṃ Huṃ-thunder-formed; Jaṃ Jaṃ Jaṃ, roar-sounding. Bhrāṃ Bhrīṃ Bhrū — Bhairavī, blessed — salutation again to Bhavānī! (Verse 7.) In simple words the thunder-seeds roll: Huṃ-formed thunder, Jaṃ-formed lion-roar, Bhr-forms of blessed Bhairavī Bhavānī — salutation and salutation.

Haṃ Saṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ Phaṭ, hail — O Rudra-formed, salutation! O honey-demon-killer, salutation! O Kaiṭabha-destroyer, salutation! O buffalo-crusher Goddess, salutation! (Verse 1, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the fire-mantra's close and the four salutations slowly: Rudra-formed, Madhu-killer, Kaiṭabha-destroyer, Mahiṣa-crusher — salutation to each.
Salutation to Śumbha-killer, and to Niśumbha-slayer, salutation! (Verse 2, Hindi.) In simple words: to the killer of Śumbha salutation, and to the slayer of Niśumbha salutation.

O great Goddess, wake my chanting and perfect it! (Verse 3, Hindi, with seed-gloss.) Combined with the Hindi gloss: Aiṃ-formed creation-natured, Hrīṃ-formed world-guarding… (continues: Klīṃ-formed desire and seed-natured Goddess, salutation; Caṇḍā-destroying Cāmuṇḍā, Yai-formed boon-giver (4); Vicce-formed, forever fear-giving, mantra-formed Goddess — salutation (5); Dhāṃ Dhīṃ-formed wife of matted Śiva; Vāṃ Vīṃ Vaṃ-formed queen of speech; Krāṃ Krīṃ Krū-formed Kālī (continues next).

'Aṃ Kaṃ Caṃ Ṭaṃ Taṃ Paṃ Yaṃ Śaṃ Vīṃ Duṃ Aiṃ Vīṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ' — break, break, kindle, kindle, hail! 'Pāṃ Pīṃ Pūṃ'-formed, You are Pārvatī the Full. 'Khāṃ Khīṃ Khūṃ'-formed, You are sky-goer (or the sky-gesture). (Verse 8.) In simple words the alphabet-seeds march: break them open, kindle them, hail! — in Pāṃ-forms You are full Pārvatī; in Khāṃ-forms You are sky-wandering (or the sky-gesture herself).

'Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ'-formed, perfect for me the Saptashatī Goddess's mantra-aims. This Kuñjikā-hymn is for mantra-waking. Never give it to the loveless; guard it hidden, Pārvatī! Whoever reads Saptashatī lacking Kuñjikā, O Goddess — no perfection comes to him, like weeping in a forest. Thus ends, in holy Rudra-yāmala's Gaurī-lore, the Kuñjikā hymn of Śiva-Pārvatī-dialogue. Om, that is truth. (Verses 8–9, seal.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: 'Śāṃ Śīṃ Śū'-formed, do my good (6); 'Huṃ Huṃ Huṃ'-thunder-formed, 'Jaṃ Jaṃ Jaṃ' lion-roaring, 'Bhrāṃ Bhrīṃ Bhrū'-formed blessed Bhairavī Bhavānī — salutation again and again (7); 'Aṃ Kaṃ Caṃ Ṭaṃ Taṃ Paṃ Yaṃ Śaṃ Vīṃ Duṃ Aiṃ Vīṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ' — break, break, kindle, kindle, hail; 'Pāṃ Pīṃ Pū'-formed You are Pārvatī the Full; 'Khāṃ Khīṃ Khūṃ'-formed You are sky-goer or sky-gesture (8); 'Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ'-formed, perfect the Saptashatī Goddess's mantra-aims for me. This Kuñjikā hymn is for waking mantras; never give it to the loveless man — guard it hidden, Pārvatī! O Goddess, whoever reads Saptashatī lacking Kuñjikā wins no perfection — like weeping in a forest. Thus ends, in holy Rudra-yāmala's Gaurī-lore, the Kuñjikā hymn of the Śiva-Pārvatī dialogue. Om, that is truth. In simple words the seal is triple-locked: wake the mantra with Kuñjikā, guard it from the faithless, and never read Saptashatī without it — else the reading echoes empty like forest-weeping.

'Śāṃ Śīṃ Śū'-formed, do my good. (Verse 6, Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi prayer: 'Huṃ Huṃ Huṃ'-thunder-formed, 'Jaṃ Jaṃ Jaṃ' lion-roaring, 'Bhrāṃ Bhrīṃ Bhrū'-formed blessed Bhairavī Bhavānī — salutation again and again (7). In simple words the seed-salutations roll on: Śāṃ-forms do my good; Huṃ-thunder, Jaṃ-roar, Bhr-forms of Bhairavī — salutation.

'Aṃ Kaṃ Caṃ Ṭaṃ Taṃ Paṃ Yaṃ Śaṃ Vīṃ Duṃ Aiṃ Vīṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ' — break, kindle, hail; Pārvatī the Full; sky-goer forms. (Verse 8, Hindi.) Combined with the Hindi fruit-note: daily dawn-reading of this hymn destroys every blocking trouble; Kuñjikā-hymn plus Goddess-hymn with Saptashatī-reading wins top perfection. Then the inner senses: killing is lust-anger-killing, charming is chosen-god-charming, mastering is mind-mastering, stilling is senses' turning from objects, expelling is freedom-aching struggle — all succeed by serving this hymn for that aim. In simple words the five fierce aims turn gentle inside: killing means killing lust-anger, charming means charming the chosen god, mastering means mastering the mind, stilling means stilling the senses, expelling means aching for freedom — serve the hymn for these, and all succeed.

The holy Goddess-Atharva-top. Om — all the gods approached the Goddess: 'Who are You, great Goddess?' (Verse 1.) In simple words the Upaniṣad opens like a play: all the gods draw near the Goddess and ask — great Goddess, who are You?

She said: I am Brahman-formed. From Me, nature-male-formed world — plus void and non-void. (Verse 2.) In simple words She answers: I am Brahman itself in form. From Me came the world of nature-and-spirit — and both the void and the non-void.

I am bliss and non-bliss. I am knowing and unknowing. Both the to-be-known Brahman and non-Brahman. I am the five gross and five subtle elements. I am the whole world. (Verse 3.) In simple words the great 'I am' roll-call begins: bliss and its absence, knowledge and its absence, the knowable and unknowable both, all elements gross and subtle — I am the entire world.

I am Veda and non-Veda. Unborn am I, and un-unborn am I. Below and… wisdom am I, unwisdom am I. And sideways am I. (Verse 4.) In simple words the paradoxes pile: scripture and non-scripture, born and unborn, wisdom and unwisdom — below, above, sideways — all directions, all opposites: I.

I move with Rudras and Vasus. I wander with Ādityas and All-gods. Both Mitra-Varuṇa I bear. Indra-Agni both, and both Aśvins. (Verse 5, the famous Vedic verse.) In simple words the ancient Ṛgvedic cry: with Rudras and Vasus I move, with sun-gods and all-gods I roam — Mitra-Varuṇa both, Indra-Agni both, both Aśvin twins — I uphold them all.

Om — all the gods went to the Goddess, crying: O great Goddess, who are You? (Verse 1, Hindi.) Combined with the tag-question: so they began asking. (Verse 1.) In simple words the devotee retells the opening: all the gods approached and asked — great Goddess, who are You? — and so the questioning began.

She said: I am Brahman-formed. From Me came the nature-male, real-unreal world. (Verse 2, Hindi.) In simple words: I am Brahman in form; from Me was born the world of nature and spirit, real and unreal both.

I am bliss and non-bliss-formed. I am wisdom and unwisdom-formed. The must-know Brahman and non-Brahman too are I. Pancified and un-pancified great elements too are I. This whole seen world is I. (Verse 3, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: Veda and non-Veda am I. Wisdom and unwisdom too am I. Unborn and un-unborn (continues next). In simple words the Hindi retelling keeps pace: bliss/non-bliss, wisdom/unwisdom, must-know Brahman/non-Brahman, elements formed/unformed — this whole seen world is I.

Nature and non-nature too am I. Below, above, sideways too am I. (Verse 4, Hindi, with glory-note.) Combined with the glory-note: the Atharvaveda sings this Goddess-Atharva-top's greatness hugely — so though not counted among Saptashatī's six limbs, reading it by Atharvaveda rule profits hugely; hence it is seated here. (Running header dust follows.) In simple words: nature and non-nature, below-above-sideways — all am I. And note why this Upaniṣad sits in this book at all: the Atharvaveda glorifies it so highly that its reading profits hugely even outside the six-limb set.

I hold Soma, Tvaṣṭā, Pūṣā and Bhaga. I hold wide-striding Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Prajāpati. (Verse 6.) In simple words the holding-roll continues: moon-juice, craftsman-god, nourisher, Fortune — I hold them; wide-striding Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Prajāpati — I hold them.

I hold wealth for the ghee-rich, well-served, soma-pressing sacrificer. I am queen, wealth-joiner of wealths, all-knowing, first of sacrifice-worthy. I birth the father on the head; my womb is in the waters within the sea. Who knows thus — wins goddess-fortune. (Verse 7.) In simple words the famous Vedic boast: I hold riches for the true sacrificer; I am queen, wealth-bringer, all-knowing, first among worshipped; I birth the father on the crown — my womb lies in the sea-waters within. Whoever knows this wins the Goddess's fortune.

Then the gods said: salutation to Goddess, to great Goddess, to Gracious — salutation forever. To Nature, to Blessed — disciplined, we bowed to Her. (Verse 8, with verse 9 quoted.) Combined with the old note: Her fire-hued, penance-blazing, sun-born, rite-fruit-tasted — to Durgā Goddess we go for shelter; to demon-killer, salutation. (Verse 9.) In simple words the gods answer with the immortal salutation: to Goddess, great Goddess, Gracious — forever salutation; to Nature, to Blessed — disciplined we bowed. Then: fire-colored, penance-blazing, sun-born, tasted in rite-fruits — to Goddess Durgā we go for shelter; demon-killer, salutation.

The gods birthed goddess Speech — Her the world-formed cattle speak. May She, milch-cow, sweet-pressing, strength-milking, come to us well-praised. (Verse 10.) In simple words the Vedic cow-prayer: the gods brought forth goddess Speech; cattle and world-beings of all forms speak Her. May She, wish-cow, sweet-pressing, strength-milking, come near us, well-praised.

I hold Soma, Tvaṣṭā, Pūṣā and Fortune. Wide-striding Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Prajāpati — I hold them. (Verse 6, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: I hold wealth for the gods' fine oblation-bringers and soma-pressing sacrificers; I am the whole world's queen, wealth-giver to seekers, Brahman-formed, first among sacrifice-gods; I make soul-formed sky and the rest; my station… (continues: holds in wisdom-mood — next). In simple words the Hindi retelling: moon, craftsman, nourisher, Fortune — I hold; wide Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Prajāpati — I hold.

…holds in wisdom-mood. Whoever knows thus wins goddess-fortune. (Verse 7, Hindi completion.) In simple words: my station is the wisdom-mood holding soul-form — whoever knows this wins the Goddess's fortune.

Then the gods said: salutation to the Goddess. To the settler of great ones in their duties, the Gracious, salutation forever. To balanced-state-formed blessed Goddess, salutation. Disciplined, we bow to Her. (Verse 8, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: fire-hued, wisdom-aglow, radiant, rite-fruit-tasted Durgā Goddess — we are Hers for shelter. Demon-killing Goddess, salutation. (Verse 9.) Then: the shining outer-voice Speech the breath-gods birthed — many-kind beings speak it. That wish-cow-like bliss-giving and food… (continues: Kālarātrī verse and Gāyatrī — next). In simple words: salutation to the duty-settling Gracious One, to balanced blessed Goddess — disciplined we bow (8); fire-hued, wisdom-blazing Durgā — we shelter in Her, demon-killer salutation (9); breath-gods' bright outer Speech, spoken by many beings, bliss-giving wish-cow… (10, continues).

Śāmbhavī, God-mother, thought, jewel-loving, ever; all-lores, Dakṣa's daughter, Dakṣa-rite-destroyer. (Verse 5.) In simple words the count marches on: Śiva's-beloved, God-mother, thought, jewel-lover, all-knowing, Dakṣa's daughter, Dakṣa-rite-breaker.
Leaf-unclad, many-hued, pink, pink-holding; silk-robed, sweet-anklet-ringing. (Verse 6.) In simple words: leaf-refusing (in penance), many-colored, rosy, rose-wearing, silk-dressed, sweet-ankleted.

Beyond-measure-valiant, fierce, lovely, gods'-lovely; forest-Durgā, elephant-goddess, Mātaṅga-sage-praised. (Verse 7.) In simple words: measureless in valor, fierce to foes, lovely, heaven's beauty, forest-fortress, elephant-goddess praised by sage Mātaṅga.

Brahmā's-power, Śiva's, Indra's, Kumāra's and Viṣṇu's too; Caṇḍikā and Vārāhī, Fortune, man-formed. (Verse 8.) In simple words the seven Mothers parade as names: Brahmā's, Śiva's, Indra's, Kumāra's, Viṣṇu's powers — plus Caṇḍikā, Vārāhī, Lakṣmī in man's form.

Spotless-uplifting, knowing, doing, daily, thought-giving; many, much-loving, all-vehicles-riding. (Verse 9.) In simple words: spotless uplifter, knower, doer, daily one, thought-giver; manifold, much-loved, riding every vehicle.

Niśumbha-Śumbha-killer, buffalo-demon-crusher; Madhu-Kaiṭabha-slayer, Caṇḍa-Muṇḍa-wiper. (Verse 10.) In simple words the demon-slayer roll-call: killer of Niśumbha-Śumbha, crusher of Mahiṣa, slayer of Madhu-Kaiṭabha, wiper of Caṇḍa-Muṇḍa.

All-demons-destroyer, all-giants-slayer; all-scriptures-formed, true, all-weapons-bearing. (Verse 11.) In simple words: destroyer of every demon, slayer of every giant, formed of all scriptures, truth itself, bearer of every weapon.

Many-weapons-handed, many-missiles-bearing; maiden, one-maiden, girl, young woman, striver. (Verse 12, with full name-gloss.) Combined with the complete gloss continuing: maiden 80, one-maiden 81, girl 82, young woman 83, striver 84 (and the gloss of 32–79 runs: God-mother 32, thought 33, jewel-loving 34, all-knowing 35, Dakṣa's daughter 36, Dakṣa-rite-breaker 37, leaf-unclad (who ate not even leaves in penance) 38, many-hued (many-colored) 39, rosy (red-hued) 40, rose-holding (wearing rose or red flowers) 41, silk-robed (silk-wearing) 42, sweet-anklet-gladdened (pleased wearing sweet-sounding anklets) 43, beyond-measure-valiant (boundlessly brave) 44, fierce (harsh to demons) 45, lovely 46, gods'-lovely 47, forest-Durgā 48, elephant-goddess 49, Mātaṅga-sage-praised 50, Brahmā's-power 51, Śiva's 52, Indra's 53, Kumāra's 54, Viṣṇu's 55, Caṇḍikā 56, Vārāhī 57, Fortune 58, man-formed 59, spotless 60, uplifting 61, knowing 62, doing 63, daily 64, thought-giving 65, manifold 66, much-loving 67, all-vehicles-riding 68, Niśumbha-Śumbha-killing 69, buffalo-demon-crushing 70, Madhu-Kaiṭabha-slaying 71, Caṇḍa-Muṇḍa-wiping 72, all-demons-destroying 73, all-giants-slaying 74, all-scriptures-formed 75, true 76, all-weapons-bearing 77, many-weapons-handed 78, many-missiles-bearing 79).

Unripe and ripe, old-mother, strength-giving; big-bellied, loose-haired, dread-formed, hugely strong. (Verse 13.) In simple words: unripe maiden and ripe woman, old mother, strength-giver; big-bellied, open-haired, dreadful-formed, mighty-strong.

Fire-flamed, fierce-faced, death-night, penance-doing; Nārāyaṇī, kindly-Kālī, Viṣṇu-illusion, water-bellied. (Verse 14.) In simple words: fire-flaming, fierce-faced, night-of-death, great in penance; Nārāyaṇī, gracious Kālī, Viṣṇu's magic, ocean-bellied.

Śiva-messenger, dreadful, endless, supreme Queen; Kātyāyanī, sun-goddess, seen-face, Brahman-voicing. (Verse 15.) In simple words: Śiva's herald, dreadful one, endless one, highest Queen; Kātyāyana's daughter, sun-goddess, visible goddess, voicer of Brahman.

Whoever daily reads aloud this eight-plus-hundred Durgā-name — nothing stands unwinnable, O Goddess, in triple worlds, O Pārvatī. (Verse 16.) In simple words the fruit begins: read these 108 Durgā-names daily aloud — and nothing in all three worlds stays unwinnable for you, O Pārvatī's devotee.

Wealth, grain, son, wife, horse, elephant too; the four aims, and at the end freedom everlasting. (Verse 17.) In simple words the shopping-list of grace: money, harvest, children, spouse, horses, elephants — duty, wealth, joy, freedom in life — and deathless freedom at the end.

Having worshipped a maiden, pictured the goddess-queen of gods — worship with supreme love, read the hundred-eight-name. (Verse 18.) In simple words the method: first worship a virgin girl, meditate the goddess-queen of gods, then love-worship and read the 108 names.

His perfection comes, O Goddess, from all the best gods too; kings turn servants, and kingdom-fortune he wins. (Verse 19, with gloss-end.) Combined with the gloss-end: maiden 80, one-maiden 81, girl 82, young woman 83, striver 84, unripe 85, ripe 86, old-mother 87, strength-giving 88, big-bellied 89, loose-haired 90, dread-formed 91, hugely-strong 92, fire-flamed 93, fierce-faced 94, death-night 95, penance-doing 96, Nārāyaṇī 97, kindly-Kālī 98, Viṣṇu-illusion 99, ocean-bellied 100, Śiva-messenger 101, dreadful 102, endless (undying) 103, supreme Queen 104, Kātyāyanī 105, sun-goddess 106, seen-face 107, Brahman-voicing 108 (verses 2–15).

O Goddess Pārvatī! Whoever daily reads aloud this hundred-eight-name of Durgā — for him nothing in all three worlds is unwinnable. (Verse 16, Hindi.) In simple words the devotee repeats the promise plainly: read daily — nothing in heaven, earth or underworld stays beyond you.

He wins wealth, grain, son, wife, horse, elephant, the four human aims — and at the end, freedom forever. (Verse 17, Hindi, with old note.) Combined with the old note: worshipping a maiden, picturing goddess-queen of gods, love-worshipping, then reading the hundred-eight-name (18); such a doer wins perfection from even the best gods (19, continues next). In simple words: money, harvest, children, spouse, horses, elephants — duty, wealth, joy, freedom in life — and deathless freedom after.

Even the best gods grant him perfection; kings become his servants; he wins kingdom-fortune. (Verse 19, Hindi.) In simple words: top gods themselves grant success; kings serve him; royal fortune is his.

With cow-essence, lac, saffron, vermilion, camphor, triple-honey — drawing the diagram duly, the rite-knowing man, ever wearing it, becomes the foe-of-tripura (Śiva-like, freedom-formed). (Verse 20, Hindi.) Combined with the old note: with cow-essence, lac, saffron, vermilion, camphor, ghee (or milk), sugar and honey, drawing the diagram duly — the rite-knowing man ever wearing it becomes Śiva-like (freedom-formed). (Verse 20.) In simple words the diagram-rite: draw Her mystic figure with eight holy substances, wear it always with knowledge — and become Śiva-like, freedom itself.

On a Tuesday new-moon midnight, the moon in hundred-physicians star — drawing and reading the hymn, he becomes wealth's home. (Verse 21.) In simple words the star-timed rite: Tuesday new-moon midnight, moon in Śatabhiṣā — draw it, read it then — and become the very home of riches.
Thus ends, in holy world-essence Tantra, the Durgā hundred-eight-name hymn. (Colophon, Hindi.) In simple words the seal: so closes the 108-name hymn of Durgā from the holy Viśvasāra Tantra.

Durgā the pain-of-hardship-quieter, remover of hardship-words… (32-name garland, with story.) Combined with the full garland and story: Durgā 1, hardship-pain-quieter 2, hardship-word-remover 3, hardship-cutter 4, hardship-doer 5, hardship-destroyer 6, hardship-uplifter 7, hardship-killer 8, hardship-taker 9, hardship-wisdom-giver 10, hardship-demon-world-wildfire 11, hard-to-reach 12, hard-to-behold 13… (Verses 1–2.) Once, Brahmā and the gods worshipped queen Durgā with flowers and many offerings; pleased, hardship-ending Durgā said: 'Gods! Pleased with your worship, ask what you will — I shall grant even the hardest to win.' Hearing Her, the gods said: 'Goddess! Our foe Mahiṣāsura, thorn of all three worlds, You killed — the whole world is well and fearless. By Your grace we won our thrones back. You are a wish-tree to devotees; we have come to Your shelter. So nothing is left for us to want — we have got everything; yet at Your command, for the world's guard we wish to ask something. O Great Queen! What is the way by which, quickly pleased, You guard a being fallen in danger? O Queen of gods! Even if wholly secret, do tell us.' So prayed, kind Durgā Goddess said: 'Hosts, hear — this mystery is top-secret and hard to win. My thirty-two-name garland destroys every danger. In all three worlds no praise equals it. It is mystery-formed. I tell it — hear…' (The garland's telling follows.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: In compassionate Night's lap, all village folk, foot-walking cows and horses, wing-flying birds and moths, need-driven travellers and hawks too sleep happily (5). O Night of consciousness-power, part from us the desire she-wolf and sin wolf; drive the lust-thief band far; then become our easy crossing — freedom-giving, blessing-making (6). O Dawn, O Night's ruling Goddess — all-spread black ignorance-dark has reached me; remove it like a debt — as giving wealth You clear devotees' debts, so giving wisdom clear this ignorance (7). O Night-Goddess, You are like a milch cow; approaching You with praise I win You over. Daughter of the supreme Sky-Self! By Your grace I have conquered lust and its foes — accept this oblation of mine too, like a chant. (Verse 8, Hindi.)

tikas.author: Pāṭhabheda-ṭippaṇī
tikas.simpleEn: Reading guide: see this meaning in Saptashatī's first chapter, verses 53 to 67.

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: Ritual manual: before and after Saptashatī reading, apply the nine-lettered mantra with its placing, touching and picturing as told below. Victory to holy Gaṇapati. 'Om — of this holy nine-lettered mantra the seers are Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra, metres gāyatrī-uṣṇik-anuṣṭup, deities Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī; seed Aiṃ, power Hrīṃ, bolt Klīṃ — the use is in chanting to please Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī.' Having read it, sprinkle water. Then chanting each placing-word below, touch head, mouth, heart, secret, both feet and navel in turn with right-hand fingers. Seer-placing, finger-placing, heart-and-limbs placing, letter-placing, direction-placing and the dawn-picture, all as told in the book. (Verses 1 of the picture-hymn follows.)

tikas.simpleEn: Old quoted verse: the Goddess who stands in all beings as patience — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 14.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: Old quoted verse: the Goddess who stands in all beings as faith — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 18.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: Old quoted verse: who as pure consciousness pervades and stands through all this world — salutation thrice and again. (Verse 28.) Then: praised by gods of old for wished shelter, and served by Indra-king day by day… (continues next).

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: Scholar's mantra-counting note: some wish 'Om salutation to Caṇḍikā' to be a separate mantra — but then the saying 'from ma-letter to ṃ-letter' would break, and which 'Goddess-said' mantra to drop stays undecided; that view too is gathered and set down in the hundred-verse garland with eight good verses.

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: Past eighty-five years of age, if even now Your grace comes not… (continues: whose shelter shall I go to — next).

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: …a bad son may be, but nowhere a bad mother. (Verse 3, Hindi.) Then: O Mother, world-Mother, never did I serve Your feet, nor offer You much wealth — yet on wretch-like me You pour matchless love. Why? Because a bad son may be born, but nowhere a bad mother. (Verse 4.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: …skull-bowl shining in hand — yet titled sole Jagadīśa. Why? How did He win such greatness? Only as fruit of wedding-custom with You — marrying You raised Him. (Verse 7.) Then: moon-faced Mother, no freedom, no glory, no wisdom, no joy I want — only let my birth pass chanting Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Śiva, Śiva, Bhavānī. (Verse 8.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: …even a fault-heaped son a mother never overlooks. (Verse 11.) Then: no sinner equals me, no sin-remover equals You — knowing this, do what is fit. (12.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Śiva said: O Goddess, You are easy for devotees to reach, and arranger of all works. If in Kali-age any way exists to fulfil wishes, tell it with effort, that is, speak it. The Goddess said: O God, out of love for You alone, the means fulfilling all wishes in Kali-age — the Ambā-praise — is being lit up by me. I shall tell it — hear. Om — of this Durgā-seven-verse hymn-mantra the seer is Nārāyaṇa, metre anuṣṭup, deities Mahākālī-Mahālakṣmī-Mahāsarasvatī; the use is in seven-verse Durgā reading to please holy Durgā. That blessed Mahāmāyā Goddess surely drags even sages' minds by force into delusion. (Verse 1.) Then: O Durgā, remembered… (continues next).

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: …three-eyed and fair — salutation to You. (Verse 3.)

tikas.author: Bhāṣya (untagged)
tikas.simpleEn: …men gone to Your shelter become shelters for others. (Verse 6.)

tikas.author: Candraprabhā
tikas.simpleEn: Śaṅkara said to Pārvatī: lotus-faced One, now I shall tell the hundred-and-eight names — hear them; by whose grace-reading alone good Durgā is pleased. Hear. (Verse 1.)

tikas.author: Pāṭhabheda-ṭippaṇī
tikas.simpleEn: Name-gloss 1–26: Om Satī 1, Sādhvī 2, Becoming-lover (loving Lord Śaṅkara) 3, Bhavānī 4, world-freeing (freeing from world-bond) 5, Noble 6, Durgā 7, Victorious 8, First 9, Three-eyed 10, Spear-bearing 11, bow-bearing 12, Bright 13, fierce-belled (fierce-voiced bell-ringing) 14, greatly penanced (heavy penance-doing) 15, Mind (thinking power) 16, Thought (knowing power) 17, I-sense (I-ness's shelter) 18, mind-formed 19, pyre 20, knowing (consciousness) 21, all-mantras-formed 22. (Continues: Being — next.)
